positive_constraints.text: Use concrete, immediately visualizable actions and objects; show inner state through speech, movement, pause, face, repetition, or play.
Keep child dialogue usually short, direct, spontaneous, and allowed to be imperfect or repetitive when excited.
Keep causal reasoning close to the immediate scene; avoid polished multi-step analysis, negotiation, or abstract summaries.
Let observation turn into play naturally without requiring the child to explain the transition.
Make the caregiver a warm participant who can wonder, laugh, mishear, join play, or not know; do not make them an answer machine.
In peer scenes, let cooperation emerge through possession, imitation, turn-taking, shared action, curiosity, or play rather than adult-style negotiation.
Use at most one concrete, playful, immediately graspable image at a time; avoid abstract conceptual layering.
Prefer one action or image per breath unit and dialogue that a parent can read without mentally rewriting.
